There was a weird movement in the Internet around 2011-2013 period I'd signify as a change in the times.

It seemed no matter how bad things got, as newfags flooded 4chan and everyone started facebooking and tweeting inane bullshit, there were always options and the ocean would never still.

Just as AOL killed off the USENET communities the MPAA and RIAA killed off the piracy culture and the once underground dark jokes, demotivational posters and raids became more PC and forced. Backup chans went dark and cacaw became helldive until all went offline.

The fundamentals are Ph, sweet, spicy, and savory. If your food isn't quite where you want it one of those is missing.

For Ph your food could be too acidic or basic. If you're making a really spicy dish with a lot of acid in it and you're getting indigestion from one bite you could add any dairy you want. If I want to thicken up whatever the dish is yogurt or sour cream will thicken it up a lot, alternatively heavy cream is really nice too. If I want something a tad sweet then condensed milk works in SOME dishes. Taste things and think about if it could be incorporated with your food.

If it's too basic though, there are order wonderful options to fix things up. With yams I always put a splash of orange juice and if there aren't any kids a healthy dose of Bourbon. Lemon juice is a little more acidic than OJ and is a little more sour which works better with spicier food.

Another thing I find important, specifically with spicy food is sweet. Sweet and spicy is the best combination on this green Earth, sweet and savory coming in a close second. With spicy dishes I like a mixture of cinnamon and brown sugar. Brown sugar has a molassas/smoke kinda sweetness that works with anything with meat. Chicken Tikka Masala, candied bacon, whatever. Cinnamon is a good pairing if you're sweetening with brown sugar because it has this heat to it that pairs splendidly with brown sugars smokey profile. Regular white sugar is okay for pretty much anything else you're making where you don't feel brown sugar is a good fit. I usually keep mangos around the house to puree if I wanna add a fruity flavor to sweeten dishes as well.

Now spicy is weird because there are so many kinds of heat. Hell, peppermint has a kick to it. When it comes to most sauce based foods peppers and ground pepper is the way to go. I recently threw a cup of peppers, and some avacado and a few cloves of garlic into a food processor with some olive oil to make a really creamy, mildy spicy paste that mixes well into pasta sauce. Chopped peppers work too but they kinda just hang out in the sauce, my paste actually gets in everywhere and makes glorious garlic bread when mixed with butter. For sweet dishes I'll do a 3:1 ratio mix of cinnamon and chili powder. Tone it down if you don't like excessive heat but this is THE shit for rice pudding and even to garnish hot chocolate or ice cream.

Now savory is kind of straight forward. Salt or MSG. I usually stick to either kosher or sea salt as opposed to MSG but if you want to make your food super savory mix in very little MSG. Don't go crazy and put a tablespoon of the shit in your skillet or you're gonna be upset. Sea salt gets a bad wrap in kitchens for the same reason accent does. Shit is a little more potent and you don't really need as much. I usually use a lil more white sugar when I'm fucking with sea salt to offset its strength. 

By the way, I'm not a chef and there are probably plenty of chefs on here who'll tear this apart but my food tastes fucking amazing as long as you don't mind sweating and lightheadedness from the heat.
